job_description: The Kings County District Attorney's Office (KCDA) is one of the largest prosecutors' offices in the country and is committed to developing and implementing innovative prosecutorial strategies that will fulfill our vision of keeping Brooklyn safe while at the same time ensuring fairness and justice for all. KCDA has an exciting opportunity to work as a Paralegal Specialist in its Bureau of Prosecutorial Innovation (Pi).  Pi makes sure the Office keeps up with technology. The Bureau trains staff at every level on the systems they use every day, on artificial intelligence, on data privacy and security, and on the digital evidence that now shows up in almost every case. Pi also works directly with trial teams to prepare digital evidence for court and keeps the office current on the law in these areas. Pi works closely with IT, Legal Training, the Digital Evidence Lab, the Virtual Currency Unit, Appeals, and bureaus across the office.  Under general supervision, with latitude for independent initiative and judgement, the prospective candidate will perform the following duties:  •	Plan and schedule Pi trainings, including live classes, workshops, short demos, office hours, and self-paced modules. •	Build and maintain the Pi library, a searchable collection of guides, checklists, short videos, recorded trainings, and legal updates. •	Use real case experience to make training practical, including how evidence comes in from NYPD and other agencies and where it tends to go wrong. •	Help trial teams get ready for Pi's pre-trial case meetings by organizing digital evidence, reviewing NYPD paperwork, and flagging gaps or inconsistencies. •	Assist with tracking of trial exhibits, timelines, and presentations and preserve copies of testimony and scripts. •	Assist in monitoring the specific technology skills needed for each position within the Office. •	Coordinate with external instructors, vendors, schools, and other prosecutors' offices. •	Handle training logistics, attendance tracking, and CLE accreditation. •	Help Pi attorneys prepare for hearings and trials. •	Help maintain dashboard for tracking of inventory and materials. •	Perform other related duties as needed.  Preferred Skills:  •	Three years of Paralegal experience in a prosecutor's office, law enforcement agency, or criminal defense setting. •	Trial preparation or investigative experience. •	Familiarity with NYPD paperwork, including complaint and arrest reports, DD5s, property vouchers, SPRINT and ICAD reports, and body-worn camera footage, etc. •	Experience organizing digital evidence such as video, phone extractions, and records returns. •	Experience running training programs or managing multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously. •	Strong writing skills and the ability to explain technical topics in plain language. •	Knowledge of Microsoft applications is necessary, Microsoft Macros and VBAs a plus. •	Knowledge of digital forensics and artificial intelligence a plus. •	Knowledge of KCDA and OCA software applications a plus. •	Ability to work independently, be assertive, highly organized, and detail oriented. •	 Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.  Candidate must meet the additional requirements:  1.	A Baccalaureate Degree from an accredited college and three years of satisfactory full-time experience working in an area related to the duties described above. 2.	An Associates Degree from an accredited college and four years of satisfactory full-time experience working in an area related to the duties described above. 3.	Candidate must meet the education and/or experience criteria which is equivalent to “1” or “2”.

job_description: The Problems You’ll Solve:  As a key member of MOERJ’s executive leadership team, the Deputy Commissioner serves as a trusted advisor to the Commissioner and provides strategic direction, executive oversight, and management of the agency’s policy, planning, programmatic, and community engagement portfolios. Reporting directly to the Commissioner, the Deputy Commissioner translates agency priorities into actionable strategies, leads multidisciplinary teams, advances cross-agency partnerships, and ensures measurable progress on citywide racial equity initiatives.  KEY DUTIES:  Executive Leadership and Agency Strategy:  •	Serve as a senior advisor to the Commissioner on agency strategy, policy priorities, organizational performance, and emerging equity issues. •	Oversee the Planning and Implementation division, establishing priorities, work plans, performance expectations, and coordinated implementation strategies. •	Identify policy opportunities, organizational risks, and barriers to execution; recommend practical solutions and executive decisions. •	Support the development and implementation of MOERJ’s strategic plan.  Citywide Racial Equity Plan and Charter Mandates:  •	Provide executive oversight of implementation, monitoring, and continued development of the Citywide Racial Equity Plan. •	Oversee responsibilities related to the racial justice City Charter amendments, including the biennial Citywide Racial Equity Plan and Taskforce on Racial Inclusion and Equity. •	Coordinate with City agencies to establish implementation milestones, track commitments, address barriers, and strengthen accountability. •	Guide development of performance indicators, reporting systems, and evaluation tools to assess progress and inform improvements. •	Oversee the development and implementation of technical assistance and equity-related trainings to City agencies to support capacity to advance equity solutions.   Policy Development and Programmatic Oversight:  •	Support the development and implementation of citywide, state, and federal policy priorities aligned with MOERJ’s mission. •	Oversee MOERJ’s programmatic portfolio across units and evaluate alignment with agency goals and community needs. •	Use research, data, and community input to identify disparities, assess policy and program effectiveness, and recommend improvements. •	Ensure coordination among policy, planning, and program teams to support consistent execution and results.  Interagency Coordination and External Relations: •	Serve as a senior liaison to City Hall, Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, agency executives, elected officials, and intergovernmental partners. •	Lead cross-agency initiatives and executive discussions to resolve implementation challenges and advance shared equity priorities. •	Support the Taskforce on Racial Inclusion and Equity and other interagency bodies, as directed by the Commissioner. •	Represent MOERJ at public hearings, cross-agency taskforces, community meetings, stakeholder forums, and media engagements, as authorized. •	Develop and maintain relationships with experts and equity practitioners within the City, as well as other jurisdictions, with the goal of promoting best practices and furthering MOERJ’s mission. •	Oversee engagement with the public and external stakeholders to center New Yorkers’ voices in policy and program design and decision-making.  Organizational Leadership and Accountability:  •	Supervise assigned senior managers and division leaders; establish clear goals, regular check-ins, and performance accountability. •	Coach and develop staff, strengthen collaboration, and promote a respectful and effective workplace. •	Monitor deliverables, implementation milestones, and results; provide regular executive briefings and corrective-action recommendations. •	Coordinate with the Chief Administrative Officer on personnel needs, budget planning, resource allocation, and operational issues affecting assigned divisions. •	Lead the development of MOERJ’s professional development agenda and equity-related trainings.  Executive Support and Special Initiatives:  •	Lead special projects and emerging priorities at the direction of the Commissioner. •	Assume designated executive responsibilities in the Commissioner’s absence, consistent with delegated authority. •	Perform other duties as assigned to advance MOERJ’s mission and effective agency operations.

job_description: The Department of Social Services (DSS) is comprised of the administrative units of the New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA) and the Department of Homeless Services (DHS).  HRA is dedicated to fighting poverty and income inequality by providing New Yorkers in need with essential benefits such as Food Assistance and Emergency Rental Assistance.  DHS is committed to preventing and addressing homelessness in New York City by employing a variety of innovative strategies to help families and individuals successfully exit shelter and return to self-sufficiency as quickly as possible.  Information Technology Services (ITS) is DSS’s technology services organization. ITS mission is to support the daily, emergent, and long-term needs of both agencies.  ITS creates and enhances the technology infrastructure and computer applications that support HRA and DHS and develops applications, including a variety of client eligibility and recertification systems, case management systems, housing systems, employment/work engagement services, revenue producing computer matches, claiming systems, and personnel systems.   Information Technology Services (ITS) is recruiting for one (1) Senior IT Architect, to function as Solution Architect, who will:  • Collaborate with M&O staff on the design and development of complex code modules and Proof of Concepts (POCs) for new design approaches to the portal and mobile applications.  • Provide oversight on overall functional and technical aspects of the COTS (Commercial Off-the-Shelf) extension standards.   • Ensure product impacts on the AHRA system are understood during design sessions.  • Lead fit/gap analysis, translating functional designs to detailed technical design for large-scale applications. The Solution Architect will interact with wider technical teams across DSS and OTI to clear system designs.  • Verify all integration points are agreed upon, documented, and aligned with the City’s technical architecture; assist in delivering non-functional requirements and supporting developers in creating secure, efficient, and compliant designs; integrating ACCESS HRA web and Mobility solutions suite with legacy or COTS applications.   • Spearhead Security Accreditation efforts for the ACCESS HRA solutions suite, ensure production releases strictly adhere to DSS/OTI security policies and standards.  • Conduct security scans (Veracode), fixing vulnerabilities, and utilizing data analytics tools like ELK.   • Provide oversight and support the App Store Review and approval process for iOS and Android releases, implement defect fixes, enhancements, and configurations for building/deploying online portals and mobile application artifacts and support ongoing AHRA testing across various environments and workstreams.   • Ensure the creation and maintenance of project technical documentation; work with teams to upgrade the AHRA solutions stack, leveraging functionality available in the latest versions of COTS products.   Hours/Shift: 9:00AM-5:00PM

job_description: The Agency You’ll Join: The New York City Mayor’s Office is responsible for overseeing city services throughout the five boroughs, coordinating public agencies and departments, and managing public property. The administration is leading the fight in making the city more affordable, reducing inequality, improving public safety, ensuring delivery of efficient and effective services, and working to make New York City’s economy stronger. We value leadership, transparency, fairness, and efficiency as we actively seek diverse talents from various sectors to join our team. For current job opportunities, visit our careers page.   The Team You’ll Work With: The Mayor’s Office Information Technology Department collaborates with other city agencies to implement IT policy, procedures, and develop secure tools/applications for use by multiple agencies. IT also partners with other departments in the Mayor’s Office to develop tools and applications that streamline processes, measure performance/metrics, and increase productivity.  The Problems You’ll Solve:  •	Design, develop, and maintain efficient, scalable, and secure web applications, APIs, and enterprise solutions using the .NET framework, modern web technologies, and the Microsoft Azure cloud stack. •	Translate complex business requirements into actionable technical designs, scalable solutions, and high-level technical blueprints in collaboration with cross-functional teams and business analysts. •	Design and implement application architectures, integrations, and data solutions that seamlessly connect enterprise systems, databases, third-party tools, RESTful APIs, cloud services, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM while maintaining data integrity and accessibility. •	Provide ongoing support, maintenance, monitoring, and enhancement of critical citywide applications, ensuring system stability, reliability, security, and uninterrupted service for users. •	Diagnose and resolve application defects, production issues, system malfunctions, and performance problems across the technology stack. Optimize applications and code to meet business requirements and service-level expectations. •	Develop and maintain automated unit and integration tests, participate in quality assurance activities, conduct code reviews, and ensure applications meet established standards for reliability, maintainability, performance, and functionality. •	Collaborate with the City's Cyber Command and relevant IT teams to ensure applications meet security accreditation, OTI compliance, data protection, and enterprise technology standards. Apply secure development practices throughout the application lifecycle. •	Maintain comprehensive technical documentation, system roadmaps, source code repositories, and deployment procedures. Gather and incorporate user feedback, provide training and application support to business teams, research emerging technologies, and recommend innovative solutions that improve operational efficiency.  About You: •	You possess strong organizational, communication, customer service, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to effectively identify and resolve application-related issues. •	You can demonstrate the ability to develop, maintain, test, and support reliable, user-focused applications and technology solutions. •	You know how to handle sensitive information and maintain confidentiality with the utmost discretion while adhering to established policies and security practices. •	You will work collaboratively with IT staff, end users, and agency personnel in a professional office environment to understand needs and deliver effective technology solutions. •	You can demonstrate adaptability, attention to detail, and a commitment to continuous learning, staying current with evolving technologies and improving application functionality and user experience.  Additional Information •	In addition to the resume, a cover letter is required to apply.

job_description: **ONLY THOSE WHO ARE PERMANENT IN THE ' CERTIFIED IT ADMINISTRATOR LAN / WAN ' TITLE WILL BE CONSIDERED, AS THERE IS AN ACTIVE CS LIST**   The mission of the New York City Police Department is to enhance the quality of life in New York City by working in partnership with the community to enforce the law, preserve peace, protect the people, reduce fear, and maintain order. The New York City Police Department strives to foster a safe and fair city through the strategic deployment of resources, focusing on both crime prevention and addressing quality-of-life concerns while building lasting community relationships.  The New York City Police Departments Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) is actively seeking a highly qualified and motivated Certified IT Administrator (LAN/WAN) IV. In this role, the candidate will play a crucial part in supporting the Department by collaborating across various ITSD Sections, ensuring seamless integration between different environments and applications. Responsibilities include leading Systems Administration Section (SAS) with planning and coordinating the implementation of cutting-edge technology.   ITSD oversees critical projects and technological initiatives within the NYPD. They maintain and enhance the department's IT infrastructure, including networks, servers, and workstations. The Certified IT Administrator (LAN/WAN) IV role is pivotal in maintaining the NYPD’s technological edge and promoting safety and effectiveness in law enforcement operations.  Serve as technical lead for the Systems Administration Section and the primary escalation point for complex incidents, outages, and root-cause analyses (RCAs). Lead post-incident reviews and drive corrective actions to prevent recurrence. - Oversee day-to-day operations of Windows Server environments, on-premises and in Azure IaaS, including monitoring, backups, and incident response; support Linux servers as needed. - Build, configure, and maintain servers to established standards across VMware (vSphere, vCenter, vSAN) and Azure. - Administer core Windows services, including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS/DHCP, and Entra ID integration. - Automate server provisioning, configuration, and routine operational tasks using VMware VCF Automation (formerly vRA/Aria Automation), PowerShell, PowerCLI, and Ansible, replacing manual work with repeatable, self-service workflows. - Monitor infrastructure health, performance, and capacity using VMware VCF Operations (formerly vROps/Aria Operations), and act on alerts and trends before they affect service. - Support patching and vulnerability remediation efforts in coordination with the patch management team. - Apply and enforce security baselines and hardening standards (CIS Benchmarks, CJIS Security Policy) across all managed servers. - Enforce ITIL practices (Incident, Problem, Change, and Configuration Management) and use ServiceNow for change approvals, operational workflows, and service tracking. - Execute disaster recovery procedures, maintain high-availability configurations, and conduct regular DR testing. - Carry out infrastructure projects, including server migrations, OS and platform upgrades, and lifecycle management. - Mentor engineers, peer-review changes and scripts, and coordinate onboarding and training to close skill gaps across the team. - Partner with engineering, network, security, and application teams to keep operations aligned with organizational goals. - Maintain accurate documentation, SOPs, and runbooks.   TO APPLY: Click the ‘Apply’ button below, or visit: http://cityjobs.nyc.gov and search for JOB ID # 810007.   WORK HOUR/ SHIFT: Varies.  ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: In compliance with federal Law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.  The City of New York offers a comprehensive benefits package including health insurance for the employee and his or her spouse or domestic partner and unemancipated children under age 26, union benefits such as dental and vision coverage, paid annual leave and sick leave, paid holidays, a pension, and optional savings and pre-tax programs such as Deferred Compensation, IRA, and a flexible spending account.

job_description: ONLY OPEN TO CITY EMPLOYEES WHO ARE PERMANENT IN THE TITLE OF COMPUTER SYSTEMS MANAGER OR WHO ARE PERMANENT IN A COMPARABLE TITLE 		 The NYC Financial Information Services Agency - Office of Payroll Administration (FISA-OPA) is seeking a highly motivated and experienced manager to oversee the Technical Services (Infrastructure) Team within the Financial Systems Division. This position is for a seasoned manager - who will have responsibility for the Open Systems Team(s), Database Administration Team, and Monitoring functions and Technical Project Management. The manager must be self-motivated with a positive attitude and must be willing to work with application and integration teams on tactical and strategic projects. The manager will have full responsibility for the high availability of all underlying infrastructure systems/services. The manager will ensure that the Financial Systems infrastructure systems/services and production data can be restored within the overall design of FISA-OPA's disaster recovery design.   Roles and Responsibilities:   Under the direction of the Deputy Executive Director of Financial Systems, the Director has the primary responsibility of:  PERFORMANCE MONITORING • Ensure that processes are in place to actively monitor online and batch operations. Monitoring will ensure that system response times are within acceptable levels. Monitoring will ensure that system resources (CPU and memory) are configured to safely support both peak and regular usage levels and that resources are assigned at a level to support planned growth with an appropriate level of support for unexpected spikes.  CAPACITY PLANNING • Ensure that periodic evaluations of storage are performed to determine if current capacity can meet planned needs or if additional storage must be allocated. The manager will work with all Financial technical teams to come up with a singular needs package that addresses the growth requirements, e.g., disk storage, memory, CPU, database licenses., etc.  NEW TECHNOLOGIES • Evaluate new hardware and system software technologies as requested - and during upgrade cycles to determine if technical strategies should be adjusted to align with external trends.  • Evaluate new hardware and system software technologies as requested - and during upgrade cycles to determine if technical strategies should be adjusted to align with external trends.   INFRASTRUCTURE SOFTWARE VERSION MANAGEMENT • Within the FMS Infrastructure team framework, ensure that processes are in place to manage the inventory of database product versions and that we remain informed about the life-cycle for the products we operate.  •Ensure that database system solutions remain on vendor supported product levels and ensure that upgrade projects are initiated in coordination with business, test, and development teams.  FISCAL PLANNING  • Within the City and FISA-OPA's budget and planning cycle, produce a plan that lays out the cost over time for hardware and software purchase / upgrades as necessitated by: end-of-Iife for hardware, new business requirements, end of support for software, capacity/growth, consolidation initiatives for cost reduction, etc.   SECURITY  • Ensure that production and non-production database, operating system and middleware tiers are securely configured to meet FISA-OPA and City standards.   • Manage authorization and authentication processes for products within the scope of the infrastructure team (OS, database, middleware access). • Provide guidance to infrastructure teams to ensure all security, provisioning, separation of duty requirements are aligned with industry standards and pass independent audit - and any audit findings have proper remediation plans in place.  INFRASTRUCTURE TEAM OVERSIGHT  • Ensure that the Open System, Database, Business Objects, Performance and Monitoring teams operate as a cohesive group to ensure that systems remain available per service level agreements with business and application teams.  • Oversee the group managers / team leads and ensure that the daily operations are monitored and issues are escalated.  • Prioritize work, plan and provide leadership to the Infrastructure teams in order to best meet the commitments and project target dates for large and small initiatives.  PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT The Director of Technical Services is responsible for the direct management, development, and accountability of the FMS Technical Services staff, including:  • Assign and prioritize work across the teams to meet operational and project demands. • Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and coaching to team members. • Establish clear expectations, deliverables, and performance standards. • Monitor work quality, timeliness, and adherence to procedures. • Conduct regular one-on-one meetings, performance evaluations, and feedback sessions. • Address performance issues in a timely and professional manner. • Support staff development, cross-training, and succession planning. • Ability to work with and communicate with team individuals to address concerns with positive enhancements for a cohesive homogeneous team environment.  Preferred Skills/Experience:  • Strong management and team leadership skills. • Demonstrated ability to establish a roadmap for operational improvement.  • Excellent troubleshooting, analytical and problem-solving skills. • Excellent communication skills (oral and written), interpersonal, and organizational and strong project management skills. • Ability to motivate staff, implement and improve processes, develop staffs' knowledge and career path, interact with senior and across team management, assess staffs' abilities and delegate and monitor work assignments. • Self-motivated with ability to work well with other groups in an enterprise wide, large-scale matrix environment. • 15+ years’ experience in IT management, multiple roles in systems implementation, supervision of technical personnel, architecture, security/compliance, and business wide strategic planning. • 15+ years’ experience managing an IBM AIX environment. • 10+ years’ experience in analysis, implementation and evaluation of IT systems and their specifications. • 10+ years’ experience in Backup and Recovery for day-to-day operations and Disaster Recovery. • 15+ years’ experience managing, installing, and upgrading of Open Systems platforms. • 5+ years’ experience supporting large Oracle database environments. • 5+ years’ experience supporting large ERP application (e.g., Oracle) or application environments. • 5+ years’ experience with Business Intelligence (e.g., Business Objects) and Data Warehouse environments. • 5+ years’ experience understanding of IBM WebSphere application server and messaging technologies. • 10+ years’ experience with Performance Analysis and Tuning, Capacity Planning. • Infrastructure architecture knowledge of FMS applications.  Additional Information   P163  To Apply   External applicants please visit https://a127-jobs.nyc.gov/ to apply to Job ID # 810960. Current NYC employees may apply via Employee Self Service (ESS). While all complete applications will be given consideration, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted by FISA-OPA.  	 Hours/Shift   35 hours Weekly/Day.

job_description: NOTE: This position is open only to the current City of New York employees serving in a permanent Civil Service title of Computer Associate (Operations) or Computer Associate (Software).  To be considered for this position, PLEASE CLEARLY INDICATE YOUR CURRENT PERMANENT CIVIL SERVICE TITLE on your resume and cover letter.  The New York City Comptroller’s Office works to promote the financial health, integrity, and effectiveness of New York City government, in order to strengthen trust, secure a thriving future for all New Yorkers, and build a more just, equitable, and resilient city. Led by an independently elected citywide official, the comptroller’s office provides checks and balances needed to hold City government accountable for budgeting wisely, investing responsibly, operating efficiently, acting fairly, living up to its obligations and promises, and paying attention to the long-term challenges we face together.  The Office of the Comptroller’s Bureau of Information Systems provides a full range of technology support services for key business functions and Charter mandated responsibilities of the Comptroller’s Office. These services include technology strategic planning, web site development, graphic design, disaster recovery, systems development, network administration, audio/visual services, business process re-engineering, change management, program management, security administration, service desk, computer operations, telecommunications, and document management.  Under the direction of the Director of IT Operations & Network Services, the Systems Administrator manages Active Directory provisioning, Office 365 administration, ATP monitoring, security administration and MS security updates.  Tasks include, but are not limited to, the following:  Microsoft Active Directory Administration •	Provide identity management functions for entire account lifecycle, including creation, modifying, and separation accounts from the environment. •	Perform and monitor security administration by modifying users, groups and application links, passwords etc. for all agency critical systems. job_description: The Agency You’ll Join: The New York City Mayor’s Office is responsible for overseeing city services throughout the five boroughs, coordinating public agencies and departments, and managing public property. The Innovation Team (I-team), within the Office of the First Deputy, focuses on mapping systems, identifying pain points, conducting user engagement, research, and rapid prototyping to develop novel, human-centered solutions for NYC's complex challenges. The I-Team works in close partnership with the Efficiency Team (E-team) to ensure that newly tested concepts and prototype solutions can be effectively integrated, scaled, and implemented across city agencies. While the I-team identifies system friction points, designs interventions, and conducts qualitative and quantitative research, in certain projects it collaborates directly with the E-team's agency integrators and systems experts to transition these innovations into sustainable operational practices and citywide policies.  The Problems You’ll Solve:  As a Data and Civic Innovation Analyst, you will provide critical support across all phases of the innovation cycle. You will assist project leaders and multidisciplinary team members in understanding complex municipal challenges and testing creative solutions.    Responsibilities include: •	Maintain project tracking logs, track and report on detailed project plans, and prepare data-driven presentations, reports, and executive summaries for senior internal and external stakeholders. •	Provide direct operational and analytical support for qualitative and quantitative research workstreams, including background research, policy synthesis, and data collection. •	Collect, analyze, and visualize quantitative and qualitative data to identify trends, draw actionable insights, and develop detailed, data-driven project plans.  •	Support ideation and co-design workshops by preparing workshop materials, capturing insights, mapping user journeys, synthesizing feedback, and documenting pain points. •	Participate in rapid prototyping and testing efforts, helping to create low-fidelity prototypes, collect user feedback, and refine proposed interventions. •	Map complex administrative systems, service delivery workflows, and agency interactions to identify cross-cutting change management needs, operational bottlenecks, and opportunities for streamlining processes.  •	Help drive inter-agency collaboration to build buy-in, proactively identify and mitigate risks, and problem-solve execution issues as they arise. •	Collaborate with the E-Team to gather baseline data, document operational requirements, and ensure seamless integration and resource optimization.  •	Support performance monitoring by tracking key metrics and assisting with the evaluation of pilot projects and prototype outcomes. •	Assist with change management efforts, helping agency partners build capacity and adapt internal processes to support long-term adoption of new workflows.  About You: You will be a part of the Innovation Team and exemplify the following: •	You are a curious, detail-oriented problem-solver with strong data and process fluency and a passion for public service, design thinking, and civic innovation. •	You are a structured thinker able to quickly build content knowledge in new policy or operational areas, translate complex issues for diverse audiences, and juggle multiple, competing priorities.  •	You possess excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience drafting summaries, slide decks, and project documentation. •	You have strong organizational skills, with a proven ability to manage multiple tasks, track project milestones, and support cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment. •	You demonstrate empathy in engaging diverse stakeholders, community members, and public sector personnel. •	You are comfortable navigating ambiguity. job_description: Job Description:  The Center for Population Health Data Science (CPHDS)- launched in October of 2023- aims to catalyze critical data modernization work and enable the agency to make progress toward linking public health, healthcare, and social service for timely and effective publication. We are working towards making these data more accessible, timely, equitable, meaningfully usable, and protected – and actively used to protect and promote the health and wellbeing of New Yorkers. We aim to strengthen agencywide data capabilities by empowering our workforce, enhancing intra- and inter-agency data sharing, and using modern technology to yield trusted and integrated data and insights. A real-time and comprehensive view of city needs is needed to enhance public health actions and improve health outcomes for the most vulnerable New Yorkers. The CPHDS is working to strengthen citywide population health surveillance by better linking public health, healthcare, and social service data to fully characterize and improve the health of New Yorkers. Our vision is for these data to be accessible, timely, equitable, meaningfully usable, and protected in order to protect and promote health and wellbeing of New Yorkers. The Bureau of Data Technology and Strategy (DTS) is dedicated to the development of the Enterprise Data Platform (EDP) and is home to data strategy, data governance, data product management, data engineering, and data science capabilities. The Applied Data Science and Solutions unit within DTS oversees a number of mission critical agency projects including the Master Patient Index project, the Client Engagement Platform project, the Whole Genome Sequencing project, and various interoperability projects to support Disease surveillance systems. The unit also provides analytical support for ad hoc analyses and admin support for the Enterprise Data Platform.   Duties will include but not be limited to:  -Develop, manage, and build integration pipelines across environments to support multiple agency initiatives. -Design and implement CI/CD-enabled data pipelines to automate and manage the promotion of updates across development, staging, and production environments. -Design and implement mechanisms for managing access and permissions for EDP resources. -Oversee development of datalake integration processes. -Advise and implement governance and permissioning in datalake environment. -Lead communication, planning, and coordination among stakeholders for projects.  Preferred Skills:  •5 or more years of Python experience  •5 or more years of SQL development experience  •5 or more years of business intelligence experience  •3 or more years of system admin experience  •3 or more years of datalake experience  •3 or more years of cloud development work  Why you should work for us:  - Benefits: City employees are entitled to unmatched benefits such as: o a premium-free health insurance plan that saves employees over $10K annually, per a 2024 assessment. o additional health, fitness, and financial benefits may be available based on the position’s associated union/benefit fund. o a public sector defined benefit pension plan with steady monthly payments in retirement. o a tax-deferred savings program and o a robust Worksite Wellness Program that offers resources and opportunities to keep you healthy while serving New Yorkers. - Work From Home Policy: Depending on your position, you may be able to work up to two days during the week from home. - Job Security - you could enjoy more job security compared to private sector employment and be able to contribute to making NYC a healthy place to live and work.  Established in 1805, the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC Health Department) is the oldest and largest health department in the U.S., dedicated to protecting and improving the health of NYC. Our mission is to safeguard the health of every resident and cultivate a city where everyone, regardless of age, background, or location, can achieve their optimal health. We provide a wide array of programs and services focused on food and nutrition, anti-tobacco support, chronic disease prevention, HIV/AIDS treatment, family and child health, environmental health, mental health, and social justice initiatives. As the primary population health strategist and policy authority for NYC, with a rich history of public health initiatives and scientific advancements, from addressing the 1822 yellow fever outbreak to the COVID-19 pandemic, we serve as a global leader in public health innovation and expertise.  Come join us and help to continue our efforts in making a difference in the lives of all New Yorkers!  The NYC Health Department is an inclusive equal opportunity employer committed to providing access and reasonable accommodation to all individuals. To request reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, contact Sye-Eun Ahn, Director of the Office of Equal Employment Opportunity, at sahn1@health.nyc.gov or 347-396-6549.

job_description: ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD   The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation. ¿   We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government.   We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust.   ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT    The Strategy, Products, and Innovation division leads the agency’s strategic planning and policy work, partnering across the agency to test and implement new ideas. The division also develops and delivers the agency’s product roadmap, maintaining and modernizing the systems that support our work in future elections.   The new Data department will ensure that the agency’s information is trustworthy, well governed, protected, and ready to use. As the agency moves to a modern cloud platform and data lakehouse and explores responsible uses of AI, the department will set the standards for how data is classified, managed, and maintained. It will bring together data governance, privacy, records management, open data, and AI assurance, and work closely with engineering teams, which build to these standards, and with staff across the agency who rely on data to do their work.   The department will be built in phases. In the near term, the Senior Director of Data will welcome the Records, Data & Information unit into the department, establish the data governance program alongside the agency’s cloud migration, and build strong workflows across these disciplines. Over the next few years, the department will grow to include a data science capability that supports the agency’s mission and strategic goals.     JOB DESCRIPTION   The NYC Campaign Finance Board is seeking an experienced and strategic Senior Director of Data (SDD) to lead the agency’s data governance, privacy, information management, records and public disclosure, and artificial intelligence (AI) assurance functions. The SDD will establish and oversee the frameworks, standards, policies, and controls necessary to ensure that agency data is trustworthy, secure, appropriately governed, legally compliant, and suitable for operational, analytical, research, and public-disclosure purposes.   This position will lead the agency’s data strategy across structured and unstructured data environments, oversee governance of the data lakehouse and cloud-migration initiatives, strengthen the agency’s privacy program, and ensure appropriate management of records and Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) production. The role will also establish an independent AI assurance function to evaluate data readiness, privacy, fairness, transparency, and accountability before AI use cases are authorized for production and while they remain operational.   The successful candidate will combine strategic leadership, sound governance judgment, technical fluency, and the ability to build new capabilities while strengthening established teams. The position works in partnership with senior leadership, data engineering, legal, records, product, and other cross-functional stakeholders.     Role Expectations   This is a strategic governance and organizational leadership position, not a hands-on data engineering role. The successful candidate must be able to establish governance standards, influence peer engineering leaders, exercise independent judgment on AI assurance, and build effective programs and teams.    Key Responsibilities     -  Develop and oversee enterprise data governance frameworks, including data classification, quality, metadata, lineage, and retention standards.     -  Establish and lead the agency’s privacy and information-governance program, including sensitive-data protection, data loss prevention (DLP), and disclosure screening.     -  Oversee records management, FOIL/public-records production, retention schedules, and proactive open-data disclosure.     -  Lead independent AI assurance reviews covering data readiness, privacy, bias, fairness, transparency, and accountability.     -  Govern data platforms, cloud migration, and data lakehouse initiatives by establishing standards and reviewing technical and vendor deliverables.     -  Partner with engineering leadership to ensure data solutions meet governance requirements while maintaining appropriate separation between governance and technical implementation.     -  Build and strengthen governance, privacy, and records functions; lead team integration, workforce planning, staff development, and performance management.     -  Develop long-term data strategy and a roadmap for future in-house data science and predictive modeling capabilities.     -  Advise executive leadership on data risks, compliance, governance priorities, and organizational strategy.     Required Qualifications     -  Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; an advanced degree in data, information management, law, public policy, or a related discipline is preferred.     -  10+ years of experience in data governance, privacy, records management, or related information-governance functions, including 5+ years of team leadership.     -  Demonstrated experience developing and implementing enterprise data governance frameworks and holding technical teams accountable to established standards.     -  Experience building or improving privacy, information-governance, records-management, or compliance programs.     -  Knowledge of AI/ML governance, data readiness, bias and fairness assessment, and responsible AI assurance.     -  Familiarity with data lakehouses, cloud governance platforms, DLP, and relevant FedRAMP/NIST-aligned requirements.     -  Strong understanding of records retention, public-records disclosure, and statutory or regulatory compliance.     -  Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder-management, documentation, and strategic planning skills.     -  Public-sector, regulated-industry, or comparable governance experience is strongly preferred.    ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs)   We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description. We believe in the power of diverse perspectives and the unique blend of lived experiences, non-traditional education pathways, practical know-how, and a variety of skills and abilities that each candidate brings to the table. If you're ready to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply and be part of our dynamic team.   Knowledge     -  Comprehensive understanding of enterprise data governance frameworks, including data classification, data quality, metadata, lineage, and retention across structured and unstructured data environments.     -  Knowledge of privacy and information governance, sensitive-information protection, data loss prevention, and regulatory compliance.     -  Understanding of records management, retention schedules, public-records disclosure, and FOIL or comparable statutory disclosure requirements.     -  Knowledge of AI/ML assurance principles, including data readiness, bias and fairness assessment, privacy, and accountability.     -  Familiarity with data lakehouse governance, cloud data platforms, and relevant FedRAMP/NIST-aligned requirements.     Skills     -  Ability to establish and implement data governance standards that technical teams can operationalize and maintain.     -  Demonstrated skill in holding engineering teams accountable to governance standards without direct reporting authority.     -  Experience building and strengthening privacy, information-governance, or records-management functions while integrating established teams.     -  Strong skills in AI assurance, risk assessment, privacy review, and evaluating governance deliverables from vendors and technical teams.     -  Excellent cross-functional collaboration, executive communication, strategic planning, documentation, and team leadership skills.     Abilities     -  Ability to build new governance capabilities while improving established programs, processes, and teams.     -  Ability to exercise independent judgment on data privacy, AI assurance, fairness, and compliance risks, even when delivery timelines create competing priorities.     -  Ability to translate complex governance and regulatory requirements into practical, documented standards and actionable policies.     -  Ability to build consensus across engineering, Legal, IT, records, and executive leadership while balancing operational needs with statutory obligations.     -  Ability to develop long-term data strategies and establish a roadmap for future data science and predictive modeling capabilities.    Other Behaviors     -  Demonstrates strong ownership, accountability, integrity, and sound professional judgment.     -  Maintains high standards of documentation, audit readiness, transparency, and defensible decision-making.     -  Demonstrates a builder mindset, taking initiative to establish new functions and improve existing operations.     -  Communicates respectfully, handles sensitive information with discretion, and fosters a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture.     -  Demonstrates a commitment to public service, responsible data use, ethical AI, and the agency’s mission.     -  Promotes a discrimination-free workplace where staff feel valued, respected, and supported.     -  Demonstrates fairness and transparency in their professional interactions, decisions, and evaluations.     -  Values and integrates diverse perspectives and experiences.    PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS     -  A bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; an advanced degree in data, information management, law, public policy, or a related field is preferred.     -  10+ years of experience in data governance, privacy, records management, or related information-governance work, including 5+ years of experience leading teams. These experience thresholds are subject to confirmation against the applicable civil service title.     -  Demonstrated experience leading data governance, information governance, privacy, or records functions, ideally spanning more than one of these areas.     -  Experience establishing governance standards that technical teams implement and holding delivery teams accountable to those standards.     -  Experience strengthening and maturing functions with statutory or compliance responsibilities.     -  Public-sector, regulated-industry, or comparable governance experience.     -  Experience building operational privacy and data-governance capabilities while integrating and developing established teams.     -  Experience with records management, retention scheduling, public-records production, and proactive disclosure workflows.     -  Knowledge of AI/ML assurance, including data readiness, bias and fairness assessment, privacy, and accountability.     -  Familiarity with data-platform governance, data lakehouse environments, centralized governance platforms such as Microsoft Purview, and FedRAMP/NIST-aligned requirements.     -  Experience evaluating strategic vendor deliverables and overseeing governance requirements for data platforms and cloud-migration initiatives.     -  Knowledge of data science and predictive modeling sufficient to scope, staff, and lead a future data science function.     -  Strong cross-divisional leadership, stakeholder-convening, and executive communication capabilities.     -  Demonstrated ability to build new functions, strengthen existing programs, and maintain high standards of documentation, defensibility, and audit readiness.

job_description: The NYC Financial Information Services Agency-Office of Payroll Administration (FISA-OPA) seeks to hire a Senior Risk Analyst. The Senior Risk Analyst will report directly to the Director of Risk Management. This individual will be responsible for identifying and documenting the risk portfolio of FISA-OPA. This includes translating technical risks to business processes, tracking and updating the KPI dashboard and when applicable, contributing to the updates of the internal Risk Framework. The individual will work closely with the various business team leads and the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to understand how business and security risks impact underlying workflow processes within the agency. job_description: NYCERS is seeking an experienced professional to serve as an Organizational Change Management (OCM) Business Readiness Specialist supporting the successful implementation and sustained adoption of the Legacy Replacement Program (LRP). Significant changes will be introduced to NYCERS business processes, technology, workflows, and how employees perform their daily responsibilities. This position will focus on ensuring the organization and its employees are prepared for the changes LRP will deliver, understand how those changes will impact their work, and have the necessary support to successfully transition to the future state. The OCM Business Specialist will serve as a critical connection between the LRP program and NYCERS business operations. The individual will proactively engage business leaders and employees to understand the impact of upcoming changes, anticipate challenges, identify readiness gaps, and help address concerns and operational issues that may arise throughout the transition. A key responsibility of this role is not only to communicate what is changing, but to understand the employee experience, anticipate challenges, and work with the business to identify practical solutions that support successful adoption.  Working in close partnership with the LRP Program Director and OCM Lead, the Business Specialist will ensure organizational readiness, business impacts, and employee adoption are considered throughout program planning, implementation, and decision-making. The position will also collaborate closely with the LRP Business Relationship Manager (BRM)/Product Owner (PO) to align business needs, solution decisions, and change management activities. This position also complements the OCM Project Manager, who is responsible for managing the OCM workplan, schedule, dependencies, and delivery activities. The Business Readiness Specialist will focus on the business-facing aspects of change, ensuring impacted divisions and employees are prepared, their concerns are understood and addressed, and business units are positioned to operate successfully in the LRP future state. Key Responsibilities  1.	Assess Business Impacts and Ensure Organizational Readiness •	Translate LRP solution, technology, and business process changes into clear, actionable impacts for NYCERS. •	Assess how future-state processes, workflows, responsibilities, and system functionality will affect existing business operations. •	Work directly with key stakeholders to evaluate organizational readiness and identify gaps before implementation. •	Identify business dependencies, operational risks, and potential challenges that may impact a successful transition. •	Partner with appropriate stakeholders to develop practical approaches to address readiness gaps and prepare business units for change. 2.	Understand and Address the Employee Change Experience •	Establish trusted relationships with business leaders, managers, and employees across impacted NYCERS divisions. •	Engage employees to understand their concerns, expectations, and challenges associated with upcoming changes. •	Anticipate issues employees may experience as they transition to new processes, systems, and ways of working. •	Work collaboratively with business stakeholders and program teams to identify solutions, address concerns, and remove barriers to adoption. •	Ensure employee feedback and operational concerns are appropriately documented, communicated, and escalated when necessary. •	Promote two-way communication so employees have opportunities to raise questions and understand how their concerns are being addressed. 3.	 Prepare Business Units for Future-State Operations •	Help business units understand what is changing, why the change is occurring, and what will be expected of them. •	Translate future-state solution capabilities into practical business scenarios and employee responsibilities. •	Identify where additional engagement, communication, training, or operational support may be needed. •	Facilitate business discussions, demonstrations, and feedback sessions to strengthen understanding and readiness. •	Partner with business leadership to prepare employees for new processes, workflows, and responsibilities. •	Identify business areas requiring additional support based on the complexity or magnitude of change. 4.	Partner with LRP Program Leadership and OCM Lead •	Work closely with the LRP Program Director and OCM Lead to align business readiness priorities with program objectives, milestones, and implementation plans. •	Provide insights into organizational impacts, employee concerns, and adoption risks that may affect successful implementation. •	Partner with the BRM/PO to understand business priorities, solution decisions, and future-state expectations. •	Ensure business feedback and readiness considerations are incorporated into appropriate program discussions and decisions. •	Coordinate with the OCM Project Manager to align business readiness needs with the overall OCM workplan and delivery. •	Support consistent messaging and coordinated engagement across the program and impacted business units. 5. Identify and Drive Resolution of Business Readiness and Adoption Issues •	Proactively identify business concerns, readiness gaps, and operational challenges associated with LRP changes. •	Work with business leaders, SMEs, the BRM/PO, and appropriate teams to identify solutions and mitigation approaches. •	Coordinate follow-up on identified concerns and ensure issues are directed to the appropriate owners for resolution. •	Monitor unresolved business readiness and adoption issues and escalate those that may affect implementation or operations. •	Maintain visibility into recurring concerns and identify opportunities for additional communication, training, or process clarification. •	Ensure business stakeholders receive appropriate follow-up and understand how their concerns are being addressed. 6. Coordinate Stakeholder Engagement, Communications, and Training Readiness •	Identify impacted stakeholder groups and assess their unique communication, engagement, and readiness needs. •	Partner with the OCM Lead, communications, and stakeholders to ensure employees receive relevant/timely information. •	Identify training and support needs based on future-state business processes and employee responsibilities. •	Gather feedback to assess whether communication and engagement activities are improving understanding and readiness. •	Work with business leaders to encourage employee participation in implementation activities, testing, and training. •	Ensure readiness concerns identified through stakeholder engagement are incorporated into OCM planning and follow-up. 7. Support Implementation, Stabilization, and Sustained Adoption •	Help business units prepare for the transition from current-state operations to the LRP future state. •	Identify potential operational disruptions or employee challenges that may arise during implementation. •	Partner with business/teams to coordinate resolution of adoption-related concerns during implementation and stabilization. •	Monitor how employees are adapting to new processes, systems, and responsibilities. •	Identify recurring challenges, process gaps, and opportunities to improve the employee experience. •	Support business leadership in reinforcing new ways of working and sustaining adoption beyond initial implementation. 8. Promote Enterprise-Wide Business Readiness •	Support a consistent approach to identifying, assessing, and addressing business impacts across NYCERS divisions. •	Identify cross-divisional dependencies and challenges that may require coordinated solutions. •	Ensure impacted business areas are appropriately engaged and their readiness needs are understood. •	Provide program leadership with visibility into organizational readiness, employee concerns, and adoption risks. •	Help ensure the organization is positioned to successfully operate in the LRP future state.  Role Accountability and Alignment: The OCM Business Specialist is responsible for driving business readiness and supporting successful employee adoption of LRP changes. The role will identify, coordinate, and drive follow-up on business readiness and adoption issues, working with appropriate business and program owners to support resolution. The position does not replace the responsibilities of the Program Director, BRM/PO, OCM Lead, or OCM Project Manager, nor does it assume ownership of technical solution design, defect resolution, or overall program delivery. Its primary focus is ensuring that the business is ready for what LRP will deliver, employees understand and can successfully navigate the changes, and concerns or barriers to adoption are proactively addressed.

job_description: The Office of the District Attorney, Bronx County (“BXDA”) is charged with the twin goals of ensuring public safety and striving for equal justice for the over 1.4 million members of the Bronx County community. job_description: Transportation Planning and Management (TPM) is responsible for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods on the City's streets, supporting the larger goals of economic and social vitality for people living, working, and doing business in New York City.  The Division’s responsibilities include planning, street design, curb management, technical analysis, signs, transit development, freight mobility and markings, and ensuring the safety of motor vehicle occupants, pedestrians, and cyclists.   The Office of Livable Streets (OLS) is tasked with prioritizing strategic planning, community engagement, research, policy, design, implementation, and long-term management. Their goal is to create streets that are livable, supporting safety, accessibility, inclusion, resiliency, active modes, community cohesion, and economic vitality citywide. Additionally, they aim to enhance New York City's pedestrian, bicycle, and micromobility networks, providing comfortable, connected, green, and reliable transportation options across the five boroughs. They place special emphasis on Priority Investment Areas, mode shift, and reimagining streets. The office also develops innovative new programs, design typologies, project delivery, and analysis tools to meet the demands of a rapidly changing population with evolving needs and technologies.  The Cycling & Micromobility (C&M) Unit is responsible for the nation’s largest network of on-street bicycle facilities (1,500+ lane-miles), enhancing street safety, and increasing bike ridership in NYC. The team’s primary focus is on innovative redesign of City streets to expand and improve the bike network.  The Cycling & Micromobility Unit seeks to hire a highly motivated and detail-oriented GIS & Data Manager to support the management, analysis, and continuous improvement of the unit's GIS datasets, project databases, and reporting systems. Under the supervision of senior staff, the selected candidate will maintain and enhance spatial and tabular data, perform GIS analysis, develop maps and visualizations, and support data-driven planning, reporting, and decision-making across the unit.  The selected candidate will coordinate with planners, engineers, designers, project managers, and partner agencies to translate transportation projects into accurate spatial data, improve data quality and reporting systems, and support the production of the official New York City Bike Map. The position will play a central role in maintaining the unit's project tracking systems and developing new tools and workflows that improve the accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility of Cycling & Micromobility data. The candidate will manage GIS datasets and project databases supporting bicycle and micromobility planning, capital project development, network tracking, and reporting. The candidate will translate transportation projects into accurate spatial and tabular data through review of engineering plans, project documents, aerial imagery, and field observations to maintain the City's authoritative bicycle network dataset. The candidate will perform GIS analysis and prepare maps, dashboards, reports, and data visualizations to support planning studies, project development, performance reporting, and executive decision-making. The candidate will coordinate with planners, engineers, designers, project managers, and partner agencies to collect, validate, and integrate project information across multiple data systems. The candidate will develop new database tools, reporting workflows, and quality control procedures that improve project tracking, network analysis, and organizational efficiency. The candidate will support production of the official New York City Bike Map and prepare maps, exhibits, and other visual materials for presentations, public outreach, and agency communications. The candidate will perform other related duties as assigned.  The Department of Transportation's (DOT) mission is to provide for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods in the City of New York and to maintain and enhance the transportation infrastructure crucial to the economic vitality and quality of life of our primary customers, City residents. DOT is an equal opportunity employer, committed to recruiting and maintaining a diverse workforce in an open and inclusive environment.

job_description: NOTE: This position is open only to City of New York employees serving in the permanent civil service title of Radio Repair Mechanic.   The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) is the largest Fire Department in the United States and universally is recognized as the world's busiest and most highly skilled emergency response agency. The Department's main goal is to provide fire protection, emergency medical care, and other critical public safety services to residents and visitors in the five boroughs.  FDNY members are sworn to serve and protect life and property and the Department works to continually educate the public in fire, life safety and disaster preparedness, along with enforcing public safety codes. Since its inception in 1865, FDNY has helped lead efforts to make New York the safest big city in the nation. This accomplishment requires a steadfast and daily commitment to maintaining the Department's core values. The Technology and Innovation Division (T&I) within the New York City Department of Design and Construction (DDC) seeks to hire a Deputy Director of Payment Systems. Partnering with client agencies, design professionals, and the construction industry, DDC manages a broad portfolio of projects—from firehouses, libraries, and community centers to roadways, sewers, and resiliency initiatives—helping to shape a more equitable, efficient, and resilient city. Through its commitment to design excellence, technological modernization, and public service, DDC ensures that critical civic projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest standards of quality.  The Technology and Innovation (T&I) Division serves as DDC’s centralized Information, Technology, and Telecom operation, organized into three core units: Network, Infrastructure and Security; Service Delivery; and Application Development. Together, these units provide the hardware, software, enterprise applications, and data ecosystem that support the agency’s daily operations. In addition to maintaining core systems, the division leads strategic modernization efforts aimed at improving efficiency, strengthening security, and advancing programmatic excellence across the agency.  Reporting to the Associate Commissioner of Application Development, the Deputy Director of Payment Systems will lead the day-to-day management of the applications and integrations that support DDC’s payment processes, from invoice and requisition intake through review, approval, and processing in the City’s financial systems. The Deputy Director will set priorities for enhancements and fixes, direct the staff and consultants supporting these systems, and serve as Application Development’s primary liaison to DDC’s finance, audit, and program units on payment technology. This role is accountable for system reliability, data integrity, and compliance with City fiscal and audit requirements, and for modernizing payment workflows to shorten processing times for DDC’s vendors and consultants. Position Overview  The Microsoft 365 Engineer is responsible for the administration, optimization, and strategic management of the organization's Microsoft 365 environment. This role will serve as the primary owner of the Microsoft 365 platform, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Microsoft Teams, and Entra ID.  The engineer will lead Microsoft 365 modernization initiatives, including migrating user and departmental data to OneDrive and SharePoint Online, implementing Microsoft 365 Copilot, and ensuring a secure, compliant, and highly available collaboration platform. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise with hands-on migration experience and the ability to drive adoption of Microsoft 365 services across the organization.  Key Responsibilities  Microsoft 365 Platform Administration: • Own and manage the organization's Microsoft 365 tenant. • Administer Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Microsoft Teams, and Entra ID. • Maintain tenant health, licensing, governance, and service configurations. • Monitor Microsoft 365 service health and proactively resolve issues.  Exchange Online Administration: • Manage mail flow, connectors, transport rules, spam and phishing protection. • Administer mailboxes, shared mailboxes, distribution lists, archive policies, and permissions. • Troubleshoot mail delivery, routing, authentication, and mailbox access issues. • Perform Exchange Online administration using both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and PowerShell. • Configure and maintain SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.  SharePoint Online & OneDrive: • Design and administer SharePoint Online sites, permissions, governance, and document libraries. • Manage OneDrive for Business configuration, storage policies, sharing settings, and lifecycle management. • Lead migration of user home drives, file shares, and departmental data to OneDrive and SharePoint Online. • Optimize collaboration and document management using Microsoft 365 best practices.  Microsoft 365 Copilot Implementation: • Lead the planning, deployment, and administration of Microsoft 365 Copilot. • Assess organizational readiness for Copilot adoption. • Configure security, permissions, and data governance required for Copilot. • Collaborate with business stakeholders to identify use cases and improve user productivity. • Provide user guidance and support for Copilot adoption.  Identity & Security: • Administer Microsoft Entra ID, including user and group management. • Configure Conditional Access, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and role-based access control (RBAC). • Support hybrid identity with Active Directory and Entra Connect. • Configure Microsoft Defender for Office 365 security policies. • Implement and maintain Microsoft Purview features including Data Loss Prevention (DLP), retention policies, sensitivity labels, and eDiscovery. • Ensure Microsoft 365 security and compliance align with organizational standards and industry best practices.  Automation & Administration • Develop and maintain PowerShell scripts to automate Microsoft 365 administration, reporting, and operational tasks. • Develop automation and integrations using Microsoft Graph PowerShell and Microsoft Graph API. • Create reports and administrative workflows for Microsoft 365 services using Microsoft Graph. • Create and maintain operational documentation, standards, and administrative procedures. • Monitor Microsoft 365 performance and recommend platform improvements.  Projects & Continuous Improvement • Lead Microsoft 365 migration and modernization projects. • Plan and execute tenant improvements and platform enhancements. • Evaluate and implement new Microsoft 365 capabilities. • Work closely with IT leadership and business teams to improve collaboration, security, and user experience. • Provide Tier 3 support and technical leadership for Microsoft 365 services. job_description: The New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA), the largest public housing authority in North America, provides decent, affordable housing for low- and moderate-income New Yorkers. NYCHA is home to 1 in 17 New Yorkers, providing affordable housing to over 500,000 authorized residents through public housing and Permanent Affordability Commitment Together (PACT) programs as well as Section 8 housing. NYCHA has nearly 200,000 apartments in over 2,400 buildings across 335 conventional public housing and PACT developments. In addition, NYCHA connects residents to critical programs and services from external and internal partners, with a focus on economic opportunity, youth, seniors, and social services. With a housing stock that spans all five boroughs, NYCHA is a city within a city.  Under direction of the Chief information Security Officer, with wide latitude for independent initiative and judgement, NYCHA is looking for an experienced manager to lead its Security Operations Center (SOC) and take it to the next level. This role is about more than keeping the lights on: the Senior Manager will mature the SOC's detection and response capabilities, drive automation to make the team faster and more consistent, and prepare NYCHA for a threat landscape increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, both by defending against AI-enabled attacks and by putting AI to work in security operations. This individual owns every security incident from detection through resolution, evaluating and assessing each event, directing the response, and keeping senior leadership informed with clear, timely updates. The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience in incident response and detection engineering, stays calm under pressure, and is a proven leader who develops their analysts and builds a collaborative team. The selected candidate will lead a team of three security analysts and report directly to the Chief Information Security Officer. If you are a seasoned cybersecurity professional with a passion for safeguarding critical infrastructure and a commitment to public service, we encourage you to apply and become a part of NYCHA's mission.  Roles and Responsibilities  •	Team Leadership: Mentor and develop SOC analysts, assign work based on skills and experience, set goals, evaluate performance, and participate in hiring as the team grows. •	SOC Operations: Direct the day-to-day operations of the SOC, including monitoring, alert triage, investigation, and escalation, and lead the response to all security incidents from detection through recovery. Assess current SOC capabilities and maintain a roadmap to mature them, tracking progress through metrics such as mean time to detect and respond. •	Leadership Communication: Provide clear and timely incident updates to senior leadership and support required regulatory and oversight reporting. •	Readiness and Continuous Improvement: Maintain incident response playbooks and procedures, run tabletop exercises, and lead post-incident reviews to identify root causes and drive changes that prevent recurrence. •	Detection Engineering and Threat Hunting: Oversee the development and tuning of detection rules, guide proactive threat hunting informed by threat intelligence, and keep detections current with evolving attacker techniques, including AI-enabled threats automate triage, enrichment, and response actions to improve speed and consistency. •	Collaboration with IT: Work closely with IT infrastructure, application, and service desk teams to investigate and remediate security events and to ensure monitoring is built into new systems.  Additional Information  1.	NYCHA employees applying for transfer, promotional, title or level change opportunities must have served a period of one year at current location and in current title and level (if applicable). 2.	NYCHA residents are encouraged to apply. 3.	NYCHA provides benefits that include a choice of medical coverage plans, deferred compensation plans and a defined pension benefit plan as a member of the New York City Employees’ Retirement System (NYCERS). job_description: The Office of the District Attorney, Bronx County ("BXDA") is charged with the twin goals of ensuring public safety and striving for equal justice for the over 1.4 million members of the Bronx County community. By "Pursuing Justice with Integrity," the BXDA places a focus on assistance for crime victims while simultaneously ensuring fairness to defendants. Moreover, the BXDA aims to balance the need to seek appropriate punishment for certain crimes while recognizing when punitive measures do not adequately advance justice. By recognizing these significant distinctions and acting accordingly, BXDA has established a standard of excellence in the representation of the Bronx community at large, which continues to grow stronger every day. In furtherance of this mission, the BXDA seeks a skilled and highly engaged Deputy Chief of Data Analytics.  The Deputy Chief of Data Analytics serves as a senior leader within the Strategic Planning & Analytics (SP&A) Bureau, supporting the Bureau Chief in advancing the Office's mission to promote fairness, effectiveness, and accountability in prosecution. The role ensures that data is leveraged to strengthen decision-making, operations, and the implementation of prosecutorial policies and initiatives.  Specific duties include but not limited to the following: - Support the Bureau Chief in shaping the Office's analytics, research, and evaluation strategy in alignment with the District Attorney's priorities. - Supervise the day-to-day work of data analysts and the ongoing development of standardized data management and analysis systems. Ensure results and products meet the highest quality standards. - Support the Bureau Chief in overseeing the translation of organizational priorities into actionable analytics and research agendas. - Provide leadership on analytic techniques specific to prosecution and criminal justice systems, including case flow, dispositions, charging, diversion programs, gun violence, domestic violence, policy and program initiatives, and other prosecutorial priorities. - Ensure that all analyses are accurate, methodologically sound, comprehensive, applicable to the context, and actionable. - Review products before dissemination to ensure quality, clarity, and applicability, particularly when findings inform policy decisions or reporting. - Work directly with legal bureaus to understand their workflows and questions. Utilize data analysis to diagnose operational issues, screening and charging patterns, or program referral challenges and work with bureaus to develop data-driven solutions. - Inform strategic policy rollouts by establishing metrics, tracking implementation, and surfacing early trends or challenges. - Ensure appropriate interpretation of trends by considering crime and policing patterns, court operations, legislative changes, and data quality issues inherent in justice-system databases.
